user.title: ClimateSync – Step 1 of 5: Heating sources
user.description: Choose climate sources, delta sensors, or a mixture. Climates contribute target minus current temperature; delta sensors supply an already calculated heating gap in **°C**, not a room temperature or a percentage. The highest positive delta controls the destination, never the sum. Missing or invalid sources contribute **0** while healthy sources continue. Select at least one source across both fields. When moving a room to a delta sensor, remove its old climate sources so they cannot overrule it. Existing selections stay unchanged until you edit them.

primary_sources.title: ClimateSync – Step 2 of 5: Primary sources
primary_sources.description: Select the rooms that may enable other rooms to piggyback on an existing heating run. The **Primary Heating Demand Active** entity uses only this subset and the same hysteresis as general demand. A secondary source can still start general heating when it is below its own target, but it will not activate the primary-demand entity.

destination.title: ClimateSync – Step 3 of 5: Destination setpoint
destination.description:
Select the thermostat ClimateSync controls and how the requested setpoint is formed. Choose **Target temperature** for ordinary climates or **Lower target temperature** for a heating-range climate; the current upper target is then preserved atomically. The maximum setpoint is a hard ceiling.

**Setback target** uses a fixed idle temperature. **Setback delta** subtracts a configurable reduction from the destination current temperature. Enter one value in the next step. Delta 0 sets the target equal to the measured temperature; the device still decides whether it needs heat.

control.title: ClimateSync – Step 5 of 5: Demand & safeguards
control.description: The activation and deactivation thresholds form one hysteresis band for both demand entities: demand starts at the higher value and remains active until it reaches the lower value. **Minimum change** is inclusive: exactly this difference is sent, while identical targets are skipped. It does not decide whether demand is active. Resync recovers missed events and the minimum send interval rate-limits writes. The activation threshold can be set from 0.001 °C. A small positive delta can activate demand while the rounded destination target remains equal to current temperature. Use a positive activation threshold and a lower deactivation threshold; zero source demand uses the configured idle policy.

setback_target.title: ClimateSync – Step 4 of 5: Fixed idle target
setback_target.description: Fixed target when demand is inactive. For example, 10 always means 10 °C. Limits follow the destination and configured safety ceiling. Input step: 0.5 °C.

setback_delta.title: ClimateSync – Step 4 of 5: Relative idle setback
setback_delta.description: Idle target = current destination temperature − setback. At 20.7 °C, 10 gives 10.7 °C and 0 gives 20.7 °C. Minimum: 0; input step: 0.5 °C. The result stays within destination limits. If current temperature is missing, the device minimum is used. Delta 0 does not guarantee zero device heat demand.

error.no_sources: Please select at least one climate source or delta sensor.
error.no_primary_sources: Please select at least one primary source.
error.primary_not_source: Every primary source must also be selected as a general source.
error.dest_is_source: The destination thermostat cannot also be a source room.
error.demand_threshold_order: The deactivation threshold must be lower than the activation threshold.
error.destination_target_unsupported: The selected destination does not currently expose the chosen target. A lower target also requires a valid upper target.
error.invalid_idle_value: Enter a finite value within the allowed limits.
error.destination_limits_unavailable: Destination limits are missing or conflict with the maximum setpoint. Check the destination.
